docs.text: HardFOC driver TMC9660 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC9660 smart motor controller. It boots the chip into parameter mode, configures BLDC, stepper and DC motors, runs field-oriented control and reads telemetry, on any MCU with SPI or UART. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes over SPI or UART and toggles four pins; it does the rest: the bootloader handshake, TMCL framing, retries, unit conversion and fault decoding. Smart gate driver with on-chip FOC TMC9660 Analog Devices (Trinamic) Motors 3-phase BLDC / PMSM, 2-phase stepper, brushed DC Control Field-oriented control on chip: torque / flux, velocity and position loops, ramps Feedback Digital Hall, ABN incremental encoder (two), SPI absolute encoder Host interface SPI mode 3 up to 10 MHz (64-bit TMCL datagrams) or UART (72-bit frames) Control pins RST, DRV_EN, WAKE (inputs), FAULTN (open-drain output) Driver modes Parameter mode (TMCL), which this driver uses; register-mode headers are included Datasheet · Parameter-mode reference · Register-mode reference · Configuration and bootstrapping What you get ¶ One object per chip. TMC9660<YourPort> exposes the chip as named subsystems: motorConfig , feedbackSense , velocityControl , positionControl , torqueFluxControl , telemetry , protection , diagnostics and more. Boot handled. bootloaderInit() resets the chip, writes the bootloader configuration and starts motor control in parameter mode. See Bootloader . Engineering units. RPM, degrees, rad/s and amperes in and out, converted with the motor's real pole pairs and sensor settings. See Units and diagnostics . A fast, correct SPI transport. NOT_READY polling instead of fixed delays, and pipelined batches: N parameter reads cost N + 1 datagrams. See Timing and throughput . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the chip's SPI and UART behaviour. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, spin a motor in about 15 lines. Hardware Pins, bus settings, control-pin levels and the evaluation kits. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: boot, configure, command, read, batch and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for tmc9660::TMC9660<MySpi> and tmcl for tmc9660::tmcl . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One TMC9660<Comm> object per chip. Its public members are the chip's subsystems; each one groups the TMCL parameters of one function and offers three levels of access: Level Example Use it for configureAuto(Config) velocityControl.configureAuto(vel) Bring-up: one struct, sensible defaults, applied in the right order Unit-aware calls setTargetVelocityRpm(1500.0, ctx) Commands and readings in RPM, degrees, rad/s Raw setters and parameters setTargetVelocityRaw(...) , writeParameter(...) Anything the chip has that a helper does not cover Member Owns motorConfig Motor type, pole pairs, PWM, commutation mode, current limits currentSensing Current-sense amplifiers, offsets and calibration gateDriver Gate-driver timing and power-stage protection feedbackSense Hall, ABN and SPI encoders torqueFluxControl Torque / flux PI loop, target torque, open-loop modes velocityControl Velocity PI loop and targets positionControl Position loop, targets and limits ramp Trapezoidal ramp generator stepDir Step / direction input referenceSearch , brake , iit , stopEvents , protection Homing, brake chopper, I²t, stop conditions, thresholds telemetry , diagnostics Readings, status and error flags, summaries script , ramDebug , nvmStorage , heartbeat , globals , gpio , power TMCL scripts, sampling, flash storage, watchdog, global parameters, chip GPIOs, hibernation Every call returns bool (or a result enum) and never throws. Check it: false means the chip did not accept the value or the transport failed. Boot the chip ¶ Nothing works until bootloaderInit() succeeds: it resets the chip, writes the bootloader configuration (clock, interfaces, feedback pins) and starts the motor-control firmware in parameter mode. #include "tmc9660.hpp" int spin_bldc_at_1000_rpm ( MySpi & spi ) { tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi > driver ( spi ); tmc9660 :: BootloaderConfig cfg {}; // 1. boot into parameter mode cfg . boot . boot_mode = tmc9660 :: bootcfg :: BootMode :: Parameter ; cfg . boot . start_motor_control = true ; if ( driver . bootloaderInit ( & cfg ) != tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi >:: BootloaderInitResult :: Success ) { return -1 ; // wiring, power or SPI mode } driver . motorConfig . setType ( tmc9660 :: tmcl :: MotorType :: BLDC_MOTOR , 7 ); // 2. motor: 7 pole pairs driver . motorConfig . setPWMFrequency ( 25000 ); const auto ctx = driver . getMotorContext (); // 3. unit conversions from the chip driver . velocityControl . setTargetVelocityRpm ( 1000.0 , ctx ); // 4. spin return 0 ; } Bootloader covers every field of BootloaderConfig , including SPI encoders and step/dir. Configure the motor ¶ Configure in this order: motor, feedback, control loops, then select the commutation mode last. The chip runs the mode as soon as you set it. Driver :: MotorConfig :: MotorProfile motor {}; motor . motorType = tmcl :: MotorType :: BLDC_MOTOR ; motor . polePairs = 7 ; motor . pwmFrequency_Hz = 25000 ; motor . maxPhaseCurrent_A = 3.0f ; // sets MAX_TORQUE and MAX_FLUX if ( ! driver . motorConfig . configureAuto ( motor )) { return false ; } Driver :: FeedbackSense :: HallConfig hall {}; // defaults: no offset, not inverted if ( ! driver . feedbackSense . configureAuto ( hall )) { return false ; } Driver :: VelocityControl :: VelocityConfig vel {}; vel . sensorSelection = tmcl :: VelocitySensorSelection :: SAME_AS_COMMUTATION ; if ( ! driver . velocityControl . configureAuto ( vel )) { return false ; } return driver . motorConfig . setCommutationMode ( tmcl :: CommutationMode :: FOC_HALL_SENSOR ); MotorProfile needs four values (type, pole pairs, PWM frequency, maximum phase current); the rest have defaults. configureAuto() returns false at the first value the chip rejects. Tune the loops afterwards with TorqueFluxConfig , VelocityConfig and PositionConfig ; Configuration lists their fields. Commutation mode When SYSTEM_OFF Default after reset; outputs off FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE , FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE First spin without feedback, encoder alignment FOC_HALL_SENSOR BLDC with digital Hall sensors FOC_ABN Incremental encoder FOC_SPI_ENC Absolute SPI encoder Command motion ¶ const auto ctx = driver . getMotorContext (); // read once, reuse for every conversion driver . velocityControl . setTargetVelocityRpm ( 1500.0 , ctx ); driver . positionControl . setTargetPositionDegMech ( 90.0 , ctx ); driver . torqueFluxControl . setTargetTorque ( 800 ); // mA driver . velocityControl . stop (); // ramp to zero, stay in the current mode driver . motorConfig . setCommutationMode ( tmcl :: CommutationMode :: SYSTEM_OFF ); The MotorContext holds what the unit conversions need: motor type, pole pairs, velocity sensor and scaling. Read it once after configuration and again only when you change one of those. Units and diagnostics explains the conversions and their limits. Read state ¶ const auto ctx = driver . getMotorContext (); double rpm = 0.0 ; if ( driver . velocityControl . getActualVelocityRpm ( rpm , ctx )) { std :: printf ( "velocity %.1f rpm 
 " , rpm ); } const float vbus = driver . telemetry . getSupplyVoltage (); // V const float temp = driver . telemetry . getChipTemperature (); // degrees C const int16_t current = driver . telemetry . getMotorCurrent (); // mA std :: printf ( "%.1f V %.1f C %d mA 
 " , vbus , temp , current ); Each read is one TMCL access (two SPI datagrams). To read several values at the same instant, batch them. Read or write several parameters at once ¶ Driver :: ParameterAccess rd [] = {{ tmcl :: Parameters :: ACTUAL_VELOCITY }, { tmcl :: Parameters :: ACTUAL_POSITION }, { tmcl :: Parameters :: GENERAL_STATUS_FLAGS }}; if ( driver . readParameters ( rd )) { // 3 accesses, 4 SPI datagrams std :: printf ( "v=%ld p=%ld 
 " , static_cast < long > ( static_cast < int32_t > ( rd [ 0 ]. value )), static_cast < long > ( static_cast < int32_t > ( rd [ 1 ]. value ))); } A batch pipelines the accesses: N reads cost N + 1 datagrams instead of 2N. Each element carries its own status . Batches accept only idempotent requests (SAP, GAP, SGP, GGP), because a lost reply makes the driver re-issue one. writeParameters() , readGlobalParameters() and writeGlobalParameters() work the same way. Use any parameter directly ¶ uint32_t maxTorque = 0 ; if ( driver . readParameter ( tmcl :: Parameters :: MAX_TORQUE , maxTorque )) { // any axis parameter ( void ) driver . writeParameter ( tmcl :: Parameters :: MAX_TORQUE , 2500 ); // mA } uint32_t loops = 0 ; ( void ) driver . readGlobal ( tmcl :: GlobalParamBank0 :: MAIN_LOOPS , loops ); // bank from the enum type Axis parameters are tmcl::Parameters ; global parameters are tmcl::GlobalParamBank0 , GlobalParamBank2 and GlobalParamBank3 , and the bank follows from the type, so an axis id cannot be sent to a global bank by mistake. The parameter-mode reference lists every parameter. Handle errors and faults ¶ tmc9660 :: diagnostics :: MotorSummary s {}; if ( driver . diagnostics . summary ( s , driver . getMotorContext ())) { if ( s . has_general_error || s . has_gate_driver_error ) { std :: printf ( "errors: general 0x%08lx gate 0x%08lx 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( s . general_error_flags ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( s . gate_driver_error_flags )); driver . telemetry . clearGeneralErrorFlags ( s . general_error_flags ); // write-1-to-clear driver . telemetry . clearGateDriverErrorFlags ( s . gate_driver_error_flags ); } } tmc9660 :: GpioSignal fault {}; if ( driver . comm (). gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: FAULTN , fault ) && fault == tmc9660 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ) { // the chip reports a severe fault or is still bootstrapping } Signal Meaning Where to look A call returns false The chip rejected the value, or the transport failed The log ( debugLog ), comm().tmclStats() has_general_error Over-current, over-temperature, supply or loop errors general_error_flags , decoded in Units and diagnostics has_gate_driver_error Short circuit, gate-drive under-voltage, bootstrap faults gate_driver_error_flags FAULTN active Bootstrapping, or a severe fault the chip latched Read the flags, fix the cause, clear them Error flags are write-1-to-clear: clear the bits you read, after you have handled the cause. A flag that comes back at once means the cause is still there. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes. Tune the transport ¶ tmc9660 :: TmclSpiTiming t {}; // datasheet defaults: no gap, 20 -> 200 us back-off, 60 polls t . maxPolls = 4 ; // in a 1 kHz control task: fail fast, mark the sample stale spi . setTmclTiming ( t ); const auto & stats = spi . tmclStats (); // frames, notReady, staleReplies, recoveries, failures ( void ) stats ; The defaults follow the datasheet: no fixed gap, NOT_READY polling with back-off, at most about 11.5 ms per access. In a fast control loop lower maxPolls so a busy chip costs you a stale sample, not a missed deadline. Timing and throughput has the cost model and the measurement app.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC9660 object, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc9660.hpp). Each subsystem turns a call into TMCL parameter reads and writes. The communication interface (SpiCommInterface or UartCommInterface in inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp) frames them, polls NOT_READY, pipelines batches and drives the control pins by name. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that moves bytes over SPI or UART, sets and reads four GPIOs and waits. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/tmc9660.hpp TMC9660 members ; inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp SpiCommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : TMC9660<Comm> and its subsystems inc/tmc9660.hpp , src/tmc9660.ipp The interface's methods only Never, for a new board Communication interface : SpiCommInterface , UartCommInterface inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp Six methods of your port Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test mocks. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant V as velocityControl participant D as TMC9660 core participant I as SpiCommInterface participant P as Your port A->>V: setTargetVelocityRpm(1000, ctx) V->>V: RPM to internal units (pole pairs, sensor) V->>D: writeParameter(TARGET_VELOCITY, value) D->>I: transferTMCL(SAP frame) I->>P: spiTransferTMCL(request) I->>P: spiTransferTMCL(reply-request), repeated while NOT_READY P-->>I: reply bytes I-->>D: TMCLReply (status, value), checksum checked D-->>V: true / false V-->>A: true / false Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: TMC9660<MySpi> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. Parameter mode and register mode ¶ The TMC9660 runs in one of two modes, chosen by the bootloader: Parameter mode (what this driver drives): the chip's firmware runs FOC and exposes TMCL parameters such as TARGET_VELOCITY and MAX_TORQUE . The host sends a few hundred bytes a second. Register mode : the host runs the control loop and writes the motion-control registers itself. The register maps are in inc/register_mode/ for reference; the driver's API does not use them. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: TMC9660<MySpi> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too.

docs.text: The TMC9660 runs in one of two modes, chosen by the bootloader: Parameter mode (what this driver drives): the chip's firmware runs FOC and exposes TMCL parameters such as TARGET_VELOCITY and MAX_TORQUE . The host sends a few hundred bytes a second. Register mode : the host runs the control loop and writes the motion-control registers itself. The register maps are in inc/register_mode/ for reference; the driver's API does not use them.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries marked BREAKING need source changes in code that used the affected API. Unreleased ¶ Breaking changes ¶ BREAKING: tmcl::Parameters no longer contains HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_CONFIG , HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_TIMEOUT , WAKE_PIN_CONTROL_ENABLE or GO_TO_TIMEOUT_POWER_DOWN_STATE . They are global bank-0 parameters and aliased axis ids ¾/10/11 (3 and 4 are MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY and COMMUTATION_MODE ), so writeParameter(HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_TIMEOUT, …) wrote the commutation mode. Use tmcl::GlobalParamBank0::… with writeGlobal() , globals.writeBank0() or the heartbeat / power subsystems. A static_assert now rejects duplicate axis ids. BREAKING: readGlobal(tmcl::Parameters, bank, …) and writeGlobal(tmcl::Parameters, bank, …) are deleted; they sent axis ids with SGP/GGP. Use the new readGlobal(GlobalParamBankN id, …) / writeGlobal(GlobalParamBankN id, …) , which deduce the bank from the enum type, or the raw uint16_t overloads. BREAKING (behaviour): writeGlobalParameter() / readGlobalParameter() return false without touching the chip when a bank enum id is passed with a different bank number. BREAKING (behaviour): the SPI handshake no longer waits a fixed 1000 µs between the request and the reply-request; it polls NOT_READY (see "Changed"). Restore the old timing with comm.setTmclTiming(tmc9660::TmclSpiTiming::legacy()) . BREAKING (behaviour): heartbeat.configureAuto({.enable = true}) arms the watchdog on the driver's own transport (SPI for an SPI comm type) instead of always on UART. Set HeartbeatConfig::interface to choose explicitly. Fixed ¶ SPI requests answered NOT_READY were silently dropped (the reference manual says the command in such a datagram is ignored); they are now re-sent. This was the cause of the " REPLY_INVALID_CMD on back-to-back transfers" symptom. SPI replies are checked against the request's opcode; a reply that belongs to another datagram is no longer returned as the answer. RamDebug::startCapture() sent type 6 ( SET_TRIGGER_MASK_SHIFT ); it now sends type 7 ( ENABLE_TRIGGER ). readData() used opcode ReadMem ; it now uses RamDebug type 9 ( READ_SAMPLE ). getStatus() reported COMPLETE as running. Heartbeat docs named bank-0 ids 10/11; they are ¾. configureHeartbeat() writes the timeout before the interface. Added ¶ TmclSpiTiming (frame gap, poll back-off, poll budget, opcode check) with setTmclTiming() / tmclTiming() , and TmclSpiStats counters. Pipelined batches: SpiCommInterface::transferTMCLBatch() (N accesses in N + 1 datagrams) and TMC9660::readParameters() , writeParameters() , readGlobalParameters() , writeGlobalParameters() , sendCommandBatch() , RamDebug::readSamples() . Full RAMDebug API: one call per Table 16 type code, Channel / Trigger / CaptureConfig , configure() / start() , getState() , getInfo() . Heartbeat::HeartbeatConfig::interface and Heartbeat::transportInterface() . Host unit tests ( -DHF_TMC9660_BUILD_TESTS=ON ) with mock SPI/UART transports, and a CI workflow. ESP32 example tmcl_timing (single vs pipelined access latency, gap sweep, histogram). Timing and throughput documentation ( docs/timing.md ). Changed ¶ Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, architecture, API guide, porting, testing), code snippets compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ , Doxygen under /api/ , versioned with mike. The Jekyll site files and the doxygen-awesome submodule are gone. setSpiRetryMaxCount() / setSpiRetryInterval() now set TmclSpiTiming::maxPolls and a fixed poll interval. The default budget is 60 re-sends with a 20 → 200 µs back-off (about 11.5 ms). With TMC9660_DISABLE_DEBUG_LOGGING , sendCommand() skips its per-access name lookup and formatting.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ The settings a TMC9660 needs before it drives a motor, in the order to apply them, with the struct for each. Most subsystems have a configureAuto(Config) call: required fields first, optional fields with defaults, values written in a safe order and verified. Use it for bring-up; the individual setters stay available for tuning. Every snippet here is compiled from tests/docs/configuration.cpp . Order ¶ Step Call Why this position 1 bootloaderInit(&cfg) Clock, interfaces and feedback pins are bootloader settings ( Bootloader ) 2 gateDriver.configurePowerStageProtection(PowerStageProfile) Timing and protection of the power stage, before any PWM 3 currentSensing.configureAuto(...) , calibrateOffsets() Offsets are measured with the motor off 4 motorConfig.configureAuto(MotorProfile) Motor type, pole pairs, PWM, current limits 5 feedbackSense.configureAuto(HallConfig / AbnConfig / SpiEncoderConfig) The sensor the loops will use 6 torqueFluxControl , velocityControl , positionControl .configureAuto(...) Loop gains and scaling 7 protection Voltage, temperature and current thresholds 8 motorConfig.setCommutationMode(...) Last: the chip starts driving as soon as it is set Current sensing ¶ Driver :: CurrentSensing :: AutoConfig cs {}; cs . shuntResistance_mOhm = 3.0f ; // from the schematic cs . expectedPeakCurrent_A = 6.0f ; // picks the amplifier gain if ( ! driver . currentSensing . configureAuto ( cs ) || ! driver . currentSensing . calibrateOffsets ( true , 2000 )) { // motor off, wait up to 2 s return false ; } Field Required Meaning shuntResistance_mOhm yes Nominal shunt value expectedPeakCurrent_A yes Highest phase current you expect; sets the amplifier gain usePeakScaling Scale for peak rather than RMS current actualShuntR_adc0_mOhm ... adc3 Measured shunt values per channel, if they differ from nominal Motor ¶ The API guide shows MotorProfile in context. Field Required Default Meaning motorType yes BLDC_MOTOR , STEPPER_MOTOR or DC_MOTOR polePairs yes BLDC: rotor pole pairs. Stepper: full steps per revolution / 4 pwmFrequency_Hz yes 20 to 25 kHz is typical maxPhaseCurrent_A yes Sets MAX_TORQUE and MAX_FLUX direction FORWARD Swap to reverse without rewiring pwmSwitchingScheme SVPWM Space-vector PWM for BLDC maxFluxCurrent_A 20 % of the phase current Flux limit outputVoltageLimit 8000 FOC output voltage limit (internal units) idlePwmBehavior PWM off when idle commutationMode unchanged Applied last, if set Control loops ¶ Driver :: TorqueFluxControl :: TorqueFluxConfig tf {}; tf . torqueP = 50 ; // unset gains keep the driver's defaults (50 / 100) tf . torqueI = 100 ; if ( ! driver . torqueFluxControl . configureAuto ( tf )) { return false ; } Driver :: VelocityControl :: VelocityConfig vel {}; vel . sensorSelection = tmcl :: VelocitySensorSelection :: DIGITAL_HALL ; vel . velocityP = 800 ; vel . velocityI = 1 ; if ( ! driver . velocityControl . configureAuto ( vel )) { return false ; } Gains are the chip's integer PI parameters. Start with the defaults, raise P until the response is fast without overshoot, then raise I to remove the steady-state error. Tune torque first, then velocity, then position. Struct Required Notable optional fields TorqueFluxConfig torqueP , torqueI , separateTorqueFluxLoops , enableFieldWeakening VelocityConfig sensorSelection velocityP , velocityI , pNormalization , iNormalization , scaling PositionConfig sensorSelection positionP , positionI , normalisation Protection ¶ driver . protection . configureVoltage ( /*over*/ 300 , /*under*/ 100 ); // 0.1 V units: 30.0 V, 10.0 V driver . protection . configureTemperature ( 100.0f , 120.0f ); // warning, shutdown in degrees C driver . protection . setOvercurrentEnabled ( true ); The voltage thresholds are in 0.1 V. Set them around your supply's real range: a 24 V system might warn at 30 V and 18 V. protection.configureAuto(ProtectionConfig) sets all of them at once. Where the defaults come from ¶ Each field's default is in its struct in inc/tmc9660.hpp and in the API reference ; the chip's own reset values are in the parameter-mode reference .

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a TMC9660, with which bus settings, and the board-level traps to avoid. All values here come from the TMC9660 datasheet (Rev. 0) and the parameter-mode reference manual . When they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins for pin numbers and active levels. Host interface pins ¶ The bootloader listens on both interfaces after power-up and answers on the one that sends it a valid command. Signal TMC9660 pin Direction Notes SPI0_MISO 1 (GPIO9) out Does not go high-Z when CS is released (see the erratum below) SPI0_MOSI 2 (GPIO10) in SPI0_SCK 3 (GPIO11) in SPI0_CS0 4 (GPIO12) in Active low; hold it low for the whole datagram UART_TX 62 (GPIO6) out Alternative to SPI UART_RX 63 (GPIO7) in Alternative to SPI The bootloader can move these functions to other pins and store the choice in OTP; see Configuration and bootstrapping . Control pins ¶ The driver addresses these pins by name ( tmc9660::TMC9660CtrlPin ) and by state ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE ). Your port maps a state to a GPIO level with the active levels you pass to its constructor, so the same driver code works with inverted or level-shifted signals. Pin Direction (chip) What it does Driver use RST in Holds the chip in reset while active Pulsed by bootloaderInit() to enter the bootloader DRV_EN in Enables the gate-driver outputs Set active before commanding motion WAKE in Wakes the chip from hibernation Kept active during operation FAULTN out, open drain Busy during bootstrapping, or a severe fault Read by bootloaderInit() and by your fault handling FAULTN needs a pull-up to the MCU's I/O voltage. RST and DRV_EN have internal pull-downs. Bus settings ¶ Setting SPI UART Mode / format Mode 3 (CPOL = 1, CPHA = 1), MSB first 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit Speed Up to 10 MHz (f SCK ); start at 1 MHz for bring-up Fixed rates or auto-baud (bootloader setting) Frame 8 bytes (64 bits) in parameter mode, 5 bytes in the bootloader 9 bytes in parameter mode, 8 in the bootloader Chip select Low for the whole frame; high time t CSH at least 4 core clocks (about 100 ns) n/a Reply Clocked out during the next datagram Follows each request The SPI reply arrives one datagram late, and a busy chip answers NOT_READY (0xF0) and ignores that datagram. The driver handles both; Timing and throughput explains how and what it costs. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant C as TMC9660 H->>C: datagram 1: request (GAP velocity) C-->>H: reply to the previous datagram (discarded) H->>C: datagram 2: reply-request FF 00 00 00 00 00 00 FF C-->>H: NOT_READY 0xF0 (busy, datagram ignored) H->>C: datagram 2 again, after a back-off C-->>H: reply to datagram 1: status 100, velocity Power ¶ Supply Range Notes VS (motor and gate driver) 7.7 V to 70 V Size the bulk capacitance for your motor current VSA (core and buck) 7.7 V to 80 V Often tied to VS VCC_IO (logic I/O) 2.5 V to 5 V Match your MCU's I/O voltage; sets the GPIO and DRV_EN levels Connect the MCU ground to the TMC9660 ground. Power the MCU before the motor supply so the control pins are driven when the chip comes up. Errata that affect the host ¶ SPI MISO stays driven after CS goes high (datasheet erratum 2) The TMC9660 does not release MISO when its chip select is de-asserted. On a bus shared with other SPI devices it corrupts their replies. Either give the TMC9660 its own SPI bus, hold it in reset while you talk to the other devices, or add a switch on MISO gated by CS (the datasheet shows an ADG719). Evaluation kits ¶ The ESP32 examples run on an ESP32-C6 DevKit with either kit: Kit Motor Feedback Document TMC9660-3PH-EVKIT 3-phase BLDC Hall, ABN encoder User guide TMC9660-STP-EVKIT 2-phase stepper ABN encoder, reference switches (Analog Devices website) The ESP32 pin assignment used by the examples lives in esp32_tmc9660_test_config.hpp . docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-mostly C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns bool or a result enum. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-tmc9660-driver.git external/hf-tmc9660-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-tmc9660-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-tmc9660-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_tmc9660 ) The hf_tmc9660 target carries the include directories and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_TMC9660_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on the driver sources HF_TMC9660_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_tmc9660/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_TMC9660_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_tmc9660 . How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_tmc9660_build_settings.cmake Sources, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt Static library for host builds and CI ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_tmc9660/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into tmc9660_version.h at configure time. Read it at run time: const char * v = tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi >:: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" Compile-time switches ¶ Define Effect TMC9660_DISABLE_DEBUG_LOGGING Removes every logDebug() call and the parameter-name lookup behind it TMC9660_LOG_TMCL_RAW_FRAMES=1 Logs every raw SPI TMCL datagram (bring-up only; slow) Next ¶ Quickstart wires the chip and spins a motor; Porting writes the communication interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the communication interface for SPI or UART. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls six methods on a class you derive from tmc9660::SpiCommInterface<Self> or tmc9660::UartCommInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp ). The base classes use CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC9660 object, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc9660.hpp). Each subsystem turns a call into TMCL parameter reads and writes. The communication interface (SpiCommInterface or UartCommInterface in inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp) frames them, polls NOT_READY, pipelines batches and drives the control pins by name. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that moves bytes over SPI or UART, sets and reads four GPIOs and waits. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/tmc9660.hpp TMC9660 members ; inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp SpiCommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method SPI UART Contract spiTransferTMCL(tx[8], rx[8]) yes One full-duplex 64-bit transfer, CS low for all 8 bytes. Return false on a bus error spiTransferBootloader(tx[5], rx[5]) yes The same for 40-bit bootloader datagrams uartSendTMCL(data[9]) yes Send one 9-byte TMCL frame uartReceiveTMCL(data[9]) yes Return true only when all 9 reply bytes are in data uartTransferBootloader(tx[8], rx[8]) yes Send 8 bytes, receive the 8-byte reply gpioSet(pin, signal) yes yes Drive RST, DRV_EN or WAKE to ACTIVE / INACTIVE gpioRead(pin, signal) yes yes Read FAULTN (and any other pin) as ACTIVE / INACTIVE delayMs(ms) , delayUs(us) yes yes Block for at least that long debugLog(level, tag, fmt, va_list) optional optional Print one line; 0 = error ... 4 = verbose SPI port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public tmc9660 :: SpiCommInterface < MySpi > { public : // Physical level of each control pin when ACTIVE: RST, DRV_EN, WAKE, FAULTN. MySpi () noexcept : SpiCommInterface < MySpi > ( true , true , false , false ) {} // One 64-bit TMCL datagram, full duplex, SPI mode 3, CS held low for all 8 bytes. bool spiTransferTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // One 40-bit bootloader datagram (used by bootloaderInit() before parameter mode). bool spiTransferBootloader ( std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // ACTIVE / INACTIVE to a GPIO level, using the active levels given to the constructor. bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( gpioOf ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( gpioOf ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: route driver logs to your logger (level 0 = error ... 4 = verbose). void debugLog ( int /*level*/ , const char * /*tag*/ , const char * /*format*/ , va_list /*args*/ ) noexcept {} private : static int gpioOf ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { switch ( pin ) { case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: RST : return 22 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: DRV_EN : return 20 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: FAULTN : return 19 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: WAKE : return 21 ; } return -1 ; } }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 3 , MSB first, up to 10 MHz. One transaction per call. CS goes low before the first byte and high after the last; never split a datagram, never merge two. No delays of your own. The driver polls the chip's NOT_READY status and backs off itself. A fixed delay in spiTransferTMCL() only makes every access slower. Timing and throughput shows the numbers. Return false only for a bus failure. Protocol errors (bad checksum, NOT_READY) are the driver's job. UART port ¶ my_uart.hpp class MyUart : public tmc9660 :: UartCommInterface < MyUart > { public : MyUart () noexcept : UartCommInterface < MyUart > ( true , true , false , false ) {} bool uartSendTMCL ( const std :: array < uint8_t , 9 >& data ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data . data (), data . size ()); } // Return true only once all 9 reply bytes are in `data`. bool uartReceiveTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 9 >& data ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read_exact ( data . data (), data . size (), 20 ); } bool uartTransferBootloader ( const std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { platform_uart_flush_rx (); return platform_uart_write ( tx . data (), tx . size ()) && platform_uart_read_exact ( rx . data (), rx . size (), 20 ); } bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( static_cast < int > ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( static_cast < int > ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void debugLog ( int , const char * , const char * , va_list ) noexcept {} }; uartReceiveTMCL() must block until it has exactly nine bytes, or fail. Returning early hands the driver a partial frame: wrong status codes, checksum errors and faults that come and go. Flush stale bytes from the receive FIFO before a bootloader exchange. Control-pin levels ¶ The constructor takes the physical level of RST, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN when each is active. The helpers signalToGpioLevel() and gpioLevelToSignal() apply them, so gpioSet() and gpioRead() stay one line each. Board RST DRV_EN WAKE FAULTN Constructor ESP32 examples, TMC9660 evaluation kits high high low low (true, true, false, false) A board with an inverting RST buffer low high low low (false, true, false, false) Change a level at run time with set_pin_active_level(pin, level) . Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_tmc9660_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF spi_master port and a UART port, with FreeRTOS delays and ESP_LOG output. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: both ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Run bootloaderInit() with retrieve_bootloader_info = true : it reads and logs the bootloader version over your port before any motor configuration. Read telemetry.getSupplyVoltage() : a plausible VS proves TMCL parameter access end to end. Watch comm.tmclStats() : failures and staleReplies should stay at zero on a healthy link. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each TMC9660 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several chips on separate ports can run in parallel.

MySpi () noexcept : SpiCommInterface < MySpi > ( true , true , false , false ) {} // One 64-bit TMCL datagram, full duplex, SPI mode 3, CS held low for all 8 bytes. bool spiTransferTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // One 40-bit bootloader datagram (used by bootloaderInit() before parameter mode). bool spiTransferBootloader ( std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // ACTIVE / INACTIVE to a GPIO level, using the active levels given to the constructor. bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( gpioOf ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( gpioOf ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: route driver logs to your logger (level 0 = error ... 4 = verbose). void debugLog ( int /*level*/ , const char * /*tag*/ , const char * /*format*/ , va_list /*args*/ ) noexcept {} private : static int gpioOf ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { switch ( pin ) { case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: RST : return 22 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: DRV_EN : return 20 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: FAULTN : return 19 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: WAKE : return 21 ; } return -1 ; } }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 3 , MSB first, up to 10 MHz. One transaction per call. CS goes low before the first byte and high after the last; never split a datagram, never merge two. No delays of your own. The driver polls the chip's NOT_READY status and backs off itself. A fixed delay in spiTransferTMCL() only makes every access slower. Timing and throughput shows the numbers. Return false only for a bus failure. Protocol errors (bad checksum, NOT_READY) are the driver's job.

docs.text: my_uart.hpp class MyUart : public tmc9660 :: UartCommInterface < MyUart > { public : MyUart () noexcept : UartCommInterface < MyUart > ( true , true , false , false ) {} bool uartSendTMCL ( const std :: array < uint8_t , 9 >& data ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data . data (), data . size ()); } // Return true only once all 9 reply bytes are in `data`. bool uartReceiveTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 9 >& data ) noexcept { return platform_uart_read_exact ( data . data (), data . size (), 20 ); } bool uartTransferBootloader ( const std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { platform_uart_flush_rx (); return platform_uart_write ( tx . data (), tx . size ()) && platform_uart_read_exact ( rx . data (), rx . size (), 20 ); } bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( static_cast < int > ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( static_cast < int > ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void debugLog ( int , const char * , const char * , va_list ) noexcept {} }; uartReceiveTMCL() must block until it has exactly nine bytes, or fail. Returning early hands the driver a partial frame: wrong status codes, checksum errors and faults that come and go. Flush stale bytes from the receive FIFO before a bootloader exchange.

docs.text: Communication protocols ¶ The four frame formats the TMC9660 speaks (bootloader and TMCL, over SPI and UART), byte by byte, with their checksums. You need this page to write a protocol analyser decoder or to debug a port at the wire level; the driver builds and checks every frame for you. Protocol Overview ¶ The TMC9660 supports two communication interfaces: - SPI : Full-duplex, high-speed, delayed replies - UART : Half-duplex, command/reply order, autobaud support Each interface has two protocols: - Bootloader Protocol : 5-byte frames (40 bits) for SPI, 8-byte for UART - Parameter Mode Protocol (TMCL) : 8-byte frames (64 bits) for SPI, 9-byte for UART Bootloader Protocol ¶ SPI Bootloader Protocol (40-bit / 5-byte) ¶ Transaction 1: SEND COMMAND ┌──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TX (5B) │ [CMD] [VALUE(32)] │ │ RX (5B) │ [PREV_STATUS] [PREV_VALUE(32)] │ └──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↓ Transaction 2: RECEIVE REPLY ┌──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TX (5B) │ [NO_OP] [0x00] [0x00] [0x00] [0x00] │ │ RX (5B) │ [STATUS] [VALUE(32)] │ └──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘ Key Features: - Frame Size: 5 bytes (40 bits) - No Bit-Flipping: Data sent and received as-is - Reply Delay: Reply to command N comes during transaction N+1 - Dummy Frame: Send all zeros to clock out reply UART Bootloader Protocol (64-bit / 8-byte) ¶ COMMAND FRAME (8 bytes): ┌────┬────┬────┬────────────────────────┬────┐ │0x55│DEVA│CMD │ VALUE (32-bit) │CRC8│ │ │DDR │ │ [MSB ... ... LSB] │ │ └────┴────┴────┴────────────────────────┴────┘ Sync Dev Cmd Byte3 Byte2 Byte1 Byte0 Checksum REPLY FRAME (8 bytes): ┌────┬────┬────┬────────────────────────┬────┐ │0x55│HOST│STAT│ VALUE (32-bit) │CRC8│ │ │ADDR│US │ [MSB ... ... LSB] │ │ └────┴────┴────┴────────────────────────┴────┘ Sync Host Stat Byte3 Byte2 Byte1 Byte0 Checksum Key Features: - Frame Size: 8 bytes (64 bits) - No Bit-Flipping: Bytes transmitted as-is - Immediate Reply: Reply comes immediately (no dummy frame needed) - CRC-8 Protection: Polynomial x⁸+x²+x¹+x⁰ over first 7 bytes - Addressing: Device address (default 1) and Host address (default 255) Parameter Mode (TMCL) Protocol ¶ SPI TMCL Protocol (64-bit / 8-byte) ¶ Command Format: ┌──────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬──────────┐ │ Byte │ 0 │ 1-2 │ 3 │ 4-6 │ 7 │ ├──────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤ │ Bits │ 0-7 │ 8-19 │ 20-23 │ 24-55 │ 56-63 │ │ Desc │ Operation│ Type │ Motor/Bank │ Data │ Checksum │ └──────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘ Reply Format: ┌──────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬──────────┐ │ Byte │ 0 │ 1 │ 2 │ 3-6 │ 7 │ ├──────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼──────────┤ │ Bits │ 0-7 │ 8-15 │ 16-23 │ 24-55 │ 56-63 │ │ Desc │ SPI Status│ TMCL Status│ Operation│ Data │ Checksum │ └──────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴──────────┘ Key Features: - Frame Size: 8 bytes (64 bits) - Reply Delay: Reply to command N is received when sending command N+1 - Checksum: 8-bit checksum over first 7 bytes - Status: SPI status byte (0xFF = OK, 0xF0 = busy); TMCL status in byte 1 (e.g. 0x64 = decimal 100 = OK) - Reply field alignment: Byte 1 is the TMCL status; byte 2 echoes the TMCL opcode. Keep those as separate bytes—do not fold part of byte 2 into the TMCL status word, or host-side isOK() checks will mis-parse good replies. - Host pacing: the chip answers NOT_READY (0xF0) while it is busy, and ignores the datagram that got that answer. SpiCommInterface::transferTMCL() re-sends it with a back-off; ports add no delays. See Timing and throughput . UART TMCL Protocol (72-bit / 9-byte) ¶ Command Format: ┌──────┬──────────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬──────────┐ │ Byte │ 0 │ 1 │ 2-3 │ 4 │ 5-8 │ 9 │ ├──────┼──────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤ │ Desc │ Sync+Address │ Command │ Type │ Motor/Bank │ Data │ Checksum │ └──────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘ Reply Format: ┌──────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬──────────┐ │ Byte │ 0 │ 1 │ 2 │ 3 │ 4-7 │ 8 │ ├──────┼──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────────┼──────────┤ │ Desc │ Host Address │ Sync+Address │ TMCL Status│ Operation│ Data │ Checksum │ └──────┴──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴──────────┘ Key Features: - Frame Size: 9 bytes (72 bits) - Immediate Reply: Reply comes immediately after command - Checksum: 8-bit checksum over first 8 bytes - Addressing: Module address in sync byte CRC & Checksum Calculations ¶ Bootloader CRC-8 (UART only) ¶ Polynomial: x⁸ + x² + x¹ + x⁰ (0x07) uint8_t calculateCRC8 ( const uint8_t * data , size_t length ) { uint8_t crc = 0 ; for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < length ; i ++ ) { crc ^= data [ i ]; for ( uint8_t bit = 0 ; bit < 8 ; bit ++ ) { if ( crc & 0x80 ) { crc = ( crc << 1 ) ^ 0x07 ; } else { crc <<= 1 ; } } } return crc ; } TMCL Checksum ¶ Simple 8-bit sum over first 7 bytes (SPI) or 8 bytes (UART): uint8_t calculateChecksum ( const uint8_t * data , size_t length ) { uint8_t sum = 0 ; for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < length ; i ++ ) { sum += data [ i ]; } return sum ; } Common Pitfalls ¶ SPI Delayed Replies ¶ Issue : Reply to command N comes during transaction N+1 Solution : the driver follows every request with a reply-request datagram ( FF 00 00 00 00 00 00 FF ) and reads the reply from it, re-sending while the chip answers NOT_READY. Batches overlap the two: datagram k carries request k and the reply to request k - 1. UART Half-Duplex Timing ¶ Issue : Must wait for complete reply before sending next command Solution : Wait for all expected bytes before sending next command: // Send command uartWrite ( command_frame , 9 ); // Wait for complete reply uint8_t reply [ 9 ]; size_t received = 0 ; while ( received < 9 ) { if ( uartAvailable ()) { reply [ received ++ ] = uartRead (); } } Checksum Errors ¶ Issue : Checksum calculation mismatch Solution : - Verify checksum algorithm matches specification - Check byte order (big-endian vs little-endian) - Ensure all bytes are included in calculation UART TMCL framing (partial reads) ¶ Issue : TMCL checksum errors, bogus status codes, or flaky reads on UART Solution : - Confirm uartReceiveTMCL only returns success after exactly nine reply bytes (see Platform Integration ). - Flush or drain stale RX data before starting bootloader or TMCL traffic if other code shares the same UART. SPI TMCL REPLY_INVALID_CMD on back-to-back transfers ¶ Issue : SPI returns SPI_STATUS=OK (0xFF) but TMCL_STATUS=REPLY_INVALID_CMD (0x02) on the second of two SPI TMCL transactions, often only when verbose logging is off . The retry loop for SPI_STATUS_NOT_READY does not catch it because the chip already considers the SPI byte-level transfer complete. Cause : The request datagram reached the chip while it was still busy and came back SPI_STATUS_NOT_READY . Per the reference manual the command in a NOT_READY datagram is ignored. Releases up to 1.0.0 did not check the status of the request datagram, so the request was dropped and the following reply-request returned the reply to the previous reply-request (status 2, invalid command). Solution : Fixed in the driver. transferTMCL() re-sends a request that comes back NOT_READY, checks that the reply echoes the request's opcode, and fails instead of returning a reply that belongs to another datagram. A post-transfer delay in spiTransferTMCL is no longer needed. See Timing and Throughput . Optional SPI wire-level TMCL logging ¶ For bench bring-up, the driver can log each SPI TMCL transaction as hex TX/RX 8-byte frames. Define TMC9660_LOG_TMCL_RAW_FRAMES to 1 before including tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp , or add -DTMC9660_LOG_TMCL_RAW_FRAMES=1 to your compile flags. Default is 0 (off) so normal runs are not flooded. Logging uses the comm adapter’s debugLog implementation. docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Spin a BLDC motor from your MCU: wire six signals, write a small port class, call five driver functions. Before you power the motor Use a current-limited supply for the first run and keep the motor free to turn. The example commands 1000 RPM as soon as the chip is up. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU TMC9660 Notes SPI SCLK, MOSI, MISO, CS SPI0_SCK, SPI0_MOSI, SPI0_MISO, SPI0_CS0 SPI mode 3, up to 10 MHz; start at 1 MHz GPIO out RST Reset; the driver pulses it in bootloaderInit() GPIO out DRV_EN Enables the gate driver outputs GPIO out WAKE Wakes the chip from hibernation GPIO in FAULTN Open drain: pull it up GND GND Common ground between the MCU and the motor supply The Hardware page has the full pin list, the evaluation-kit headers and the electrical limits. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_tmc9660 CMake target (or include inc/ and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-tmc9660-driver.git external/hf-tmc9660-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It moves bytes over SPI, sets and reads the four control pins and waits. Replace the four platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public tmc9660 :: SpiCommInterface < MySpi > { public : // Physical level of each control pin when ACTIVE: RST, DRV_EN, WAKE, FAULTN. MySpi () noexcept : SpiCommInterface < MySpi > ( true , true , false , false ) {} // One 64-bit TMCL datagram, full duplex, SPI mode 3, CS held low for all 8 bytes. bool spiTransferTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // One 40-bit bootloader datagram (used by bootloaderInit() before parameter mode). bool spiTransferBootloader ( std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // ACTIVE / INACTIVE to a GPIO level, using the active levels given to the constructor. bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( gpioOf ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( gpioOf ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: route driver logs to your logger (level 0 = error ... 4 = verbose). void debugLog ( int /*level*/ , const char * /*tag*/ , const char * /*format*/ , va_list /*args*/ ) noexcept {} private : static int gpioOf ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { switch ( pin ) { case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: RST : return 22 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: DRV_EN : return 20 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: FAULTN : return 19 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: WAKE : return 21 ; } return -1 ; } }; The constructor arguments are the physical level of RST, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN when each is active. Get them from your schematic: inverters and level shifters change them. Porting explains each method and shows the UART variant. 4. Spin the motor ¶ main.cpp #include "tmc9660.hpp" int spin_bldc_at_1000_rpm ( MySpi & spi ) { tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi > driver ( spi ); tmc9660 :: BootloaderConfig cfg {}; // 1. boot into parameter mode cfg . boot . boot_mode = tmc9660 :: bootcfg :: BootMode :: Parameter ; cfg . boot . start_motor_control = true ; if ( driver . bootloaderInit ( & cfg ) != tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi >:: BootloaderInitResult :: Success ) { return -1 ; // wiring, power or SPI mode } driver . motorConfig . setType ( tmc9660 :: tmcl :: MotorType :: BLDC_MOTOR , 7 ); // 2. motor: 7 pole pairs driver . motorConfig . setPWMFrequency ( 25000 ); const auto ctx = driver . getMotorContext (); // 3. unit conversions from the chip driver . velocityControl . setTargetVelocityRpm ( 1000.0 , ctx ); // 4. spin return 0 ; } What each step does: bootloaderInit() resets the chip, sends the bootloader configuration and starts the motor-control firmware in parameter mode. Nothing else works until it returns Success . setType() and setPWMFrequency() tell the chip what it drives. Use the pole-pair count from the motor's datasheet. getMotorContext() reads the settings the unit conversions need (pole pairs, sensor, scaling) from the chip. setTargetVelocityRpm() converts RPM to the chip's internal unit and writes the target velocity. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check bootloaderInit() returns Failure SPI mode 3, CS held low for the whole 8-byte frame, RST active level Every reply is 0x00 or 0xFF MISO wiring, a common ground, the chip's supply Motor hums but does not turn Pole pairs, phase wiring, commutation mode and feedback ( API guide ) FAULTN stays active Supply under-voltage, gate-driver fault ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : configure feedback and control loops, read telemetry, handle errors. docs.text: The port is the only platform code. It moves bytes over SPI, sets and reads the four control pins and waits. Replace the four platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public tmc9660 :: SpiCommInterface < MySpi > { public : // Physical level of each control pin when ACTIVE: RST, DRV_EN, WAKE, FAULTN. MySpi () noexcept : SpiCommInterface < MySpi > ( true , true , false , false ) {} // One 64-bit TMCL datagram, full duplex, SPI mode 3, CS held low for all 8 bytes. bool spiTransferTMCL ( std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 8 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // One 40-bit bootloader datagram (used by bootloaderInit() before parameter mode). bool spiTransferBootloader ( std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& tx , std :: array < uint8_t , 5 >& rx ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx . data (), rx . data (), tx . size ()); } // ACTIVE / INACTIVE to a GPIO level, using the active levels given to the constructor. bool gpioSet ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { return platform_gpio_write ( gpioOf ( pin ), signalToGpioLevel ( pin , signal )); } bool gpioRead ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool level = false ; if ( ! platform_gpio_read ( gpioOf ( pin ), level )) { return false ; } signal = gpioLevelToSignal ( pin , level ); return true ; } void delayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void delayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: route driver logs to your logger (level 0 = error ... 4 = verbose). void debugLog ( int /*level*/ , const char * /*tag*/ , const char * /*format*/ , va_list /*args*/ ) noexcept {} private : static int gpioOf ( tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { switch ( pin ) { case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: RST : return 22 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: DRV_EN : return 20 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: FAULTN : return 19 ; case tmc9660 :: TMC9660CtrlPin :: WAKE : return 21 ; } return -1 ; } }; The constructor arguments are the physical level of RST, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN when each is active. docs.text: Timing and throughput ¶ This page explains what one TMCL parameter access costs over SPI, which settings change it, and how pipelined batches cut the cost. It separates what the vendor specifies , what is derived from that, and what still has to be measured on hardware. What the chip specifies ¶ From the TMC9660 Parameter Mode Reference Manual (Rev. 0, "Serial-Peripheral Interface", Tables 3–5) and the TMC9660 datasheet ("SPI Peripheral — Electrical Characteristics"). Both PDFs are in docs/datasheet/ . Fact Source A 64-bit request's reply is clocked out during the next datagram Reference manual, SPI section SPI_STATUS_NOT_READY (0xF0): the chip is busy, the reply in this datagram is not the reply you want, and the command in this datagram was ignored . Re-send the datagram until the status goes away Reference manual, SPI section and Table 5 fSCK ≤ 10 MHz, SPI mode 3 Datasheet, SPI peripheral CS_ high time tCSH ≥ 4 × T_CLK (about 100 ns) Datasheet, SPI peripheral Minimum request processing time / turnaround Not specified So the protocol has a ready indication (NOT_READY) and no documented minimum delay. Releases up to 1.0.0 nevertheless waited a fixed 1000 µs between the request and the reply-request datagram, and ignored NOT_READY on the request datagram. That second point also explains the old " REPLY_INVALID_CMD on back-to-back transfers" symptom (see Communication Protocols ): a request that arrived while the chip was still busy was dropped, and the reply-request then returned the reply to the previous reply-request (status 2, invalid command). What the driver does now ¶ SpiCommInterface::transferTMCL() (one access): Send the request. If the answer is NOT_READY, the request was ignored: back off and send it again. Wait TmclSpiTiming::frameGapUs (default 0 µs ). Send the reply-request FF 00 00 00 00 00 00 FF . While the answer is NOT_READY, has status 0x00, a bad checksum, or (with verifyReplyOpcode ) does not echo the request's opcode, back off and send it again. A well-formed reply that echoes 0xFF means the real reply was lost, and the access fails at once instead of returning the wrong frame. The back-off starts at pollIntervalUs (20 µs) and doubles up to pollIntervalMaxUs (200 µs), for at most maxPolls (60) re-sends: about 11.5 ms worst case. That bound is for thread context. Lower maxPolls in a high-priority control task. SpiCommInterface::transferTMCLBatch() and the driver helpers readParameters() , writeParameters() , readGlobalParameters() and writeGlobalParameters() pipeline : datagram k carries request k and clocks out the reply to request k − 1, and a final reply-request collects the last reply. N accesses cost N + 1 datagrams. The reply carried by the first datagram belongs to whatever ran before and is discarded. NOT_READY means "this datagram was ignored": it is re-sent, nothing is skipped or doubled. A stale reply (0x00, bad checksum, wrong echo) leaves it unknown whether the request in that datagram ran. The previous element is re-issued as a single access and the pipeline restarts at the current element, which may then run twice. Batches therefore accept only idempotent requests (SAP, GAP, SGP, GGP, RAMDebug reads). TmclSpiStats::recoveries counts this. Configuring it ¶ tmc9660 :: TmclSpiTiming t {}; // datasheet defaults: no gap, 20→200 µs back-off, 60 polls t . frameGapUs = 30 ; // only if a measurement shows the chip needs it t . maxPolls = 4 ; // e.g. in a 1 kHz control task: fail fast, mark the sample stale comm . setTmclTiming ( t ); comm . setTmclTiming ( tmc9660 :: TmclSpiTiming :: legacy ()); // behaviour of releases up to 1.0.0 const auto & s = comm . tmclStats (); // frames, notReady, staleReplies, recoveries, failures The older setSpiRetryMaxCount() / setSpiRetryInterval() still work. They set maxPolls , and a fixed interval (no back-off). Batched reads: using Drv = tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MySpi > ; Drv :: ParameterAccess rd [] = { { tmcl :: Parameters :: ACTUAL_VELOCITY }, { tmcl :: Parameters :: ACTUAL_POSITION }, { tmcl :: Parameters :: GENERAL_STATUS_FLAGS }}; if ( driver . readParameters ( rd )) { /* rd[i].value, rd[i].status */ } Drv :: GlobalParameterAccess g [] = { { tmcl :: GlobalParamBank0 :: MAIN_LOOPS } }; // bank 0 from the type ( void ) driver . readGlobalParameters ( g ); Defining TMC9660_DISABLE_DEBUG_LOGGING also removes the per-access parameter-name lookup and string formatting in sendCommand() . Batches never run that code. Cost per access: before and after ¶ Notation: T_f = one 64-bit datagram including the host driver's per-transaction overhead, T_p = the chip's processing time for a request (not specified, to be measured). Formula 10 MHz, T_f ≈ 20 µs 1 MHz, T_f ≈ 80 µs Before (1.0.0 + hf-core handler: 1000 µs gap, 200 µs post-delay) 2·T_f + 1000 + 200 ≈ 1.24 ms ≈ 1.36 ms Before, 6 accesses 6 × above ≈ 7.4 ms ≈ 8.2 ms After, single, chip keeps up (T_p ≤ T_f) 2·T_f ≈ 40 µs ≈ 160 µs After, pipelined batch of 6 (T_p ≤ T_f) 7·T_f ≈ 140 µs ≈ 560 µs After, pipelined batch of 8 (T_p ≤ T_f) 9·T_f ≈ 180 µs ≈ 720 µs After, single, T_p = 50 µs (one or two polls) ≈ 3·T_f + 20 ≈ 80 µs (T_p < T_f) After, batch of 6, T_p = 50 µs, no gap ≈ 6·(2·T_f + 20) + T_f ≈ 380 µs (T_p < T_f) After, batch of 6, T_p = 50 µs, frameGapUs = 30 ≈ 6·(T_f + 30) + T_f ≈ 320 µs (T_p < T_f) Every number in this table is derived, not measured. T_f ≈ 20 µs at 10 MHz assumes 6.4 µs of clocking plus about 10–15 µs of ESP-IDF transaction overhead. The "before" row matches the Vortex observability design's estimate (scenario A, 1.24 ms). The host unit tests check the datagram counts and waits of each formula on a mock chip with a virtual clock, which is not a timing measurement. Measuring it ¶ The ESP32 example tmcl_timing measures it on hardware: cd examples/esp32 ./scripts/build_app.sh tmcl_timing Release ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor tmcl_timing Release For the legacy profile and for frame gaps of 1000, 500, 250, 100, 50, 25, 10 and 0 µs (all with NOT_READY polling), it prints single-read and pipelined batch-of-6 and batch-of-8 latency (min / p50 / p99 / max and a histogram), the transport counters, value mismatches against known patterns in bank-2 user variables 0–7, and G0:12 MAIN_LOOPS . A profile is usable when mismatch and fail are both 0. Repeat with the motor in open-loop and FOC under load before picking a default for a control loop. Firmware-serviced SPI replies have been seen to stall for milliseconds under FOC load on the bench.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a TMC9660, their causes and the fix for each. Start with comm().tmclStats() and the log of a failing call: they tell transport problems (no reply, stale replies) apart from configuration problems (the chip answers but rejects the value). Datasheet-vs-driver math errata ¶ The driver's unit conversions were audited against the TMC9660 Parameter Mode and Register Mode reference manuals (May 2026). One bug was found and fixed: Ramp acceleration scaling — earlier driver versions wrote (rpm/s × k_RPM) directly to the RAMP_AMAX/A1/A2/DMAX/D1/D2 registers (NR 54..59). The chip's actual scaling is RAMP_A_register = (dV_internal/dt) × 2^17 / fCLK (Parameter Mode manual p. 72; Register Mode manual p. 44). With the default fCLK = 40 MHz the missing factor is 2^17 / 40e6 ≈ 0.0032768 , so a request of N RPM/s was previously executing at roughly N × 305 RPM/s. accelerationToInternal() now applies the correct factor and AccelerationUnit::Internal is the raw RAMP_A register integer. COMMUTATION_MODE enum values — the actual chip values are FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE = 3 and FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE = 4 (NR 4 in the Parameter Mode manual). Older internal notes had these swapped/offset; the C++ enum class CommutationMode is and has been correct. OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE range — NR 47 is 0..16383 (14-bit duty cycle, 16383 = 100 %). Older driver doc-comments listed 0..32767. The chip does not current-limit voltage mode, so use a low value (≈ 5 % = 800) for unloaded startup. Open-loop spin: rotor moves slowly while ACTUAL_VELOCITY reads correct ¶ Symptom ¶ The chip is in FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE , the ramp is configured and running, ACTUAL_VELOCITY reads back the commanded RPM, but the rotor visibly turns at a small fraction of that — sometimes 5–20% — and the shaft feels "notchy" or "stutter-y". Cause ¶ In FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE the chip injects a pure d-axis current at the commanded electrical angle. Pull-out torque on a PM rotor is bounded by T_max = K_t · Id at 90° elec lag. When inertia + cogging + bearing friction exceed that ceiling, the rotor falls behind, slips a pole pair, and recovers — average mechanical speed collapses. ACTUAL_VELOCITY does not measure the rotor in this mode. With VELOCITY_SENSOR_SELECTION = SAME_AS_COMMUTATION it is derived from the integrated phi_e ramp, so it always echoes whatever the chip is commanding — not what the rotor is doing. Confirming rotor speed requires Hall, ABN, or SPI-encoder feedback (or an external tachometer). Fix ¶ Use FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE for unloaded / lightly-loaded startup. Voltage mode applies a fixed |U| at the rotating phi_e angle; Iq emerges naturally from V − back_EMF as the rotor lags, so both d- and q-axis current flow and pull-out torque is much higher at low speed. namespace tmcl = tmc9660 :: tmcl ; driver . torqueFluxControl . setOpenloopVoltage ( 800 ); // ≈5 % modulation driver . motorConfig . setCommutationMode ( tmcl :: CommutationMode :: FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE ); Other mitigations: Lower the ramp slope ( AMAX ) so torque demand stays inside the pull-out limit. Raise OPENLOOP_CURRENT (current mode) within MAX_FLUX headroom. Add real feedback (Hall / ABN / SPI encoder) and switch to closed-loop FOC, where stator current is locked at 90° to rotor flux for maximum torque per amp. Bootloader Initialization Fails ¶ Symptom ¶ bootloaderInit() returns BootloaderInitResult::Failure Solutions ¶ Check Hardware Reset Ensure RST pin is properly toggled Verify FAULTN pin monitoring during reset Wait at least 100ms after reset Verify Communication Interface Check SPI/UART wiring Verify CS pin (SPI) or TX/RX pins (UART) Confirm clock speed ≤ 4 MHz (SPI) Check Bootloader Configuration // CRITICAL: Must set boot mode to Parameter cfg . boot . boot_mode = tmc9660 :: bootcfg :: BootMode :: Parameter ; Verify Power Supply Ensure stable power to TMC9660 Check the motor supply is within 7.7 V to 70 V No Reply from Device ¶ Symptom ¶ Communication timeouts, no response to commands Solutions ¶ SPI Issues Verify MOSI/MISO not swapped Check CS pin polarity (active LOW) Confirm SPI mode 3 (CPOL = 1, CPHA = 1) Reduce the clock to 1 MHz while bringing up Do not add delays in spiTransferTMCL() : the driver polls NOT_READY itself. REPLY_INVALID_CMD on back-to-back transfers was a bug of releases up to 1.0.0 ( Communication protocols ) On a shared SPI bus, the TMC9660 keeps driving MISO after CS goes high ( Hardware ) UART Issues Verify TX/RX pins not swapped Check baud rate matches configuration Ensure GPIO pins match bootloader config Try autobaud mode For TMCL, confirm the UART adapter reads a full 9-byte reply per transaction; partial reads produce checksum and status errors (see Platform Integration ) Check Connections Verify all connections are secure Check for loose wires Verify common ground Motor Not Starting ¶ Symptom ¶ Motor configured but not rotating Solutions ¶ Verify Bootloader Initialization // Must initialize bootloader first cfg . boot . start_motor_control = true ; docs.text: The driver's unit conversions were audited against the TMC9660 Parameter Mode and Register Mode reference manuals (May 2026). One bug was found and fixed: Ramp acceleration scaling — earlier driver versions wrote (rpm/s × k_RPM) directly to the RAMP_AMAX/A1/A2/DMAX/D1/D2 registers (NR 54..59). The chip's actual scaling is RAMP_A_register = (dV_internal/dt) × 2^17 / fCLK (Parameter Mode manual p. 72; Register Mode manual p. 44). With the default fCLK = 40 MHz the missing factor is 2^17 / 40e6 ≈ 0.0032768 , so a request of N RPM/s was previously executing at roughly N × 305 RPM/s. accelerationToInternal() now applies the correct factor and AccelerationUnit::Internal is the raw RAMP_A register integer. COMMUTATION_MODE enum values — the actual chip values are FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE = 3 and FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE = 4 (NR 4 in the Parameter Mode manual). Older internal notes had these swapped/offset; the C++ enum class CommutationMode is and has been correct. OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE range — NR 47 is 0..16383 (14-bit duty cycle, 16383 = 100 %). Older driver doc-comments listed 0..32767. The chip does not current-limit voltage mode, so use a low value (≈ 5 % = 800) for unloaded startup.

Open-loop spin: rotor moves slowly while ACTUAL_VELOCITY reads correct

docs.text: The chip is in FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE , the ramp is configured and running, ACTUAL_VELOCITY reads back the commanded RPM, but the rotor visibly turns at a small fraction of that — sometimes 5–20% — and the shaft feels "notchy" or "stutter-y".
docs.title: Symptom

docs.text: In FOC_OPENLOOP_CURRENT_MODE the chip injects a pure d-axis current at the commanded electrical angle. Pull-out torque on a PM rotor is bounded by T_max = K_t · Id at 90° elec lag. When inertia + cogging + bearing friction exceed that ceiling, the rotor falls behind, slips a pole pair, and recovers — average mechanical speed collapses. ACTUAL_VELOCITY does not measure the rotor in this mode. With VELOCITY_SENSOR_SELECTION = SAME_AS_COMMUTATION it is derived from the integrated phi_e ramp, so it always echoes whatever the chip is commanding — not what the rotor is doing. Confirming rotor speed requires Hall, ABN, or SPI-encoder feedback (or an external tachometer).
docs.title: Cause

docs.text: Use FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE for unloaded / lightly-loaded startup. Voltage mode applies a fixed |U| at the rotating phi_e angle; Iq emerges naturally from V − back_EMF as the rotor lags, so both d- and q-axis current flow and pull-out torque is much higher at low speed. namespace tmcl = tmc9660 :: tmcl ; driver . torqueFluxControl . setOpenloopVoltage ( 800 ); // ≈5 % modulation driver . motorConfig . setCommutationMode ( tmcl :: CommutationMode :: FOC_OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE_MODE ); Other mitigations: Lower the ramp slope ( AMAX ) so torque demand stays inside the pull-out limit. Raise OPENLOOP_CURRENT (current mode) within MAX_FLUX headroom. Add real feedback (Hall / ABN / SPI encoder) and switch to closed-loop FOC, where stator current is locked at 90° to rotor flux for maximum torque per amp.
